bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 5368-5393

read.skipped: reference list skimmed for lineage only

question: How can the research on eliciting reasoning from language models through prompting be organised, compared and summarised?
contributions: First survey of recent progress in reasoning with language model prompting, organised by a taxonomy of methods (strategy enhanced vs knowledge enhanced)
In-depth comparison of methods by language model, prompt source and training scenario, with discussion
Open resources, benchmark overview and future directions

results.claim: CoT prompting yields no gain, and may hurt, below roughly 100B parameters.
results.setup: Discussion of Wei et al. 2022b results (GSM8K, Fig 7); CoT is described as an emergent ability of scale
results.quote: However, when the model scale declines to less than 100B, CoT prompting will yield no performance gain and may even be detrimental.

results.claim: PaLM-62B beats LaMDA-137B with CoT, suggesting pre-training data quality matters beyond parameter count (survey's speculation).
results.setup: GSM8K and CommonsenseQA CoT results read from Figs 7 and 9, reported from Wei et al. 2022b
results.quote: PaLM-62B (Chowdhery et al., 2022) even performs better than LaMDA-137B (Thoppilan et al., 2022), possibly because it was trained on the higher-quality corpus.

results.claim: At the same parameter scale Codex (code-davinci-002) outperforms GPT-3 (text-davinci-002) with CoT; the survey suggests code pre-training may trigger CoT reasoning.
results.source: Wei et al., 2022b; Zhou 2023; Li 2022d; Zhang 2023b; Madaan 2022
results.setup: Figs 7 and 9 at 175B; footnote 3 maps Codex to code-davinci-002 and GPT-3 to text-davinci-002
results.note: Cause called 'still elusive'; a hypothesis, not a measurement

results.claim: CoT helps only when training data has local structure; simple statistical estimators can match it for frequently co-occurring variables.
results.setup: Theoretical and synthetic study cited by the survey
results.quote: Prystawski and Goodman (2023) finds that CoT is beneficial only when the training data exhibits local structure.

results.claim: Survey's reading: CoT only works on large LMs whichever way the prompt is produced; smaller LMs work by fine-tuning with rationales.
results.setup: Comparison across manual, LM-generated and retrieved prompts in Table 1
results.quote: CoT prompting only works on large LMs. Smaller LMs work by fine-tuning with rationales.

results.claim: ChatGPT answers a GSM8K item with a correct reasoning process but fails a Last Letter Concatenation item despite describing the task accurately.
results.setup: One hand-picked example per task (GSM8K, CommonsenseQA, Last Letter Concatenation) on ChatGPT, no counts
results.quote: it fails to answer the given question, showing that its symbolic reasoning ca- pability is not as excellent as the above two
results.note: Anecdotal single cases; text has a hyphenated line break 'ca-pability'

results.claim: The survey notes the ChatGPT GSM8K output matches GSM8K gold format, suggesting contamination.
results.setup: Single GSM8K test case on ChatGPT
results.quote: indicating that GSM8K may be contained in the training corpus of ChatGPT

limits: Survey covers mostly 2022 work from ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, NeurIPS, ICLR, arXiv; may miss references and technical detail (Limitations).
Benchmark task boundaries may be inaccurate; omits generics, default inheritance and non-monotonic reasoning.
Conclusions are speculation from existing empirical work and 'may not be macroscopic enough' (Limitations).
Scale/emergence claims are quoted from Wei et al. 2022b with no new experiments; only anecdotal ChatGPT cases are new.
Dated: predates ReAct-era agent surveys, o1-style reasoning models; planning/agents appear only through Reflexion, Toolformer, ART, Chameleon.
practices: Prefer larger LMs for CoT: below ~100B it gives no gain (Sec 4.1).
Choose prompt source by task: manual for simple templates/few-shot, LM-generated for per-question rationales, retrieved for stability at higher IR cost (Sec 4.2).
Use code interpreters (PAL, PoT) to separate computation from reasoning for robustness and interpretability (Sec 3.1.3, 6).
Use ensemble/sampling (self-consistency, step-aware voting) rather than relying on one brittle prompt (Sec 3.1.2).
Decompose complex problems into multi-stage prompts (Least-to-Most, Self-Ask) (Sec 3.1.1).

terms.definition: one stage refers to one input-output process; single-stage improves the quality of prompt T, multi-stage appends c_i to the context or designs T_ci per step
self: an extra module calibrates one reasoning process; ensemble: multiple processes assembled into the answer; iterative: fine-tune the LM on generated (Q,C,A) triplets
physical simulator (prompt producer), code interpreter (reasoning executor), or tool learning (tool extender)
knowledge generated by the LM as prompt (implicit 'modeledge') vs retrieved from external corpus (explicit)
